restrictions: Ordinary collision of SHA-256 reduced to 39 steps from the standard IV: two 128-byte messages with the same random first block M0 and second blocks M1, M1' = M1 + DL (differences in words 8..12), then the common padding block. The second block is the transplanted advice pair with A[6], A[7] released over a list generated at import by rule on the fibre h4 = 0x3cc9eebe: 9,701,592 entries in 728 classes, 3,462,264 (a2, W10) keys; the walk constants c9, C9 are shifted by 0x05cefde0. The W17 condition is solved per F9 claw by a generic bit-sliced pass over the 62,400 distinct 18-bit prefixes; a passing prefix is completed, tested on scalar words and, at a key hit, expanded to the classes of its group.

Refile of 9054e0c4 (mitchuski) on Jbenisek's valid ae2d3c1c (credited; our 0b62ed88 with 0xplemonade's a3eb4a8a screen, credited): the program, the screen, the screened whole-window H6 method and the fourth-decimal ceiling are kept; ae2d3c1c's tail is not used. Trials are F8-passing entries, 10701.9 per distinct claw (99% on 10,000 claws of 80 screened windows); K = 10,369 from 124 screened windows; the entries tail 2^-74.4783 is the lower of the pooled and class-01 means of the 14 organizer-executed r39-mate runs; the mate term eps/2 = 0.000099 from an exhaustive rows-18-19 enumeration under the named premise H-W3-uniform, tested by the organizer (0 of 1,888 hits with W3 in the bad sets); without the premise the time would be 94.1648. Divisor 1 - 0.073047; time 94.0683 (ceiled); pass 143,633, setup 1,107,473,556; memory 2^20.0000 (peak 1,013,609 bytes plus 32,768).

heuristics.statement: MODEL (declared, new in this entry). Under the screened chaining-value and window law of the shipped program (a3eb4a8a screen S <= 5, KCAP = 679, DTRY = 8,192, KTRY = 32; windows of 2^26 walk evaluations): (i) distinct claws per window have mean 57,012.41, the unit C_W of B and the cap (124-window panel mean, s.d. 214.29); (ii) [not used by this entry: trials are measured on screened windows]; (iii) kept chaining values are independent across windows; the (a0, a1) of the distinct F9 claws of a window are i.i.d., independent of the chaining value and of the number of claws, and a claw's trial-key count is a function of its (a0, a1) only (W8..W11 do not depend on the chaining value); the W17 claw constants (w, c) are uniform and independent of (a0, u), as H5 uses; at most 1,024 distinct F9 claws are evaluated per window (program cap; at most 959 in the 124 screened windows). In this entry the trial count is measured on screened windows (proof Section 7) and is not part of this premise.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target sha256-r39-prefix-v1 and the --attack path of experiments/r39joint_k4.py (screen on) with the shipped advice pair and the list generated at import.
heuristics.extrapolation: Trials are not carried by this premise in this entry: measured on 10,000 F9 claws of 80 screened 2^26 windows of the shipped program (10701.9 F8-passing entries per distinct claw at 99%; one-way ANOVA of the claws' entry counts over the 80 windows F = 1.175 on 79 and 9,920 df). C_W = 57,012.41 is the mean of 124 screened windows (ae2d3c1c's 60 and this entry's 64).
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run: the screened windows (ae2d3c1c 60, this entry 80) and the claw counts.

heuristics.statement: The W17 pass costs exactly 143,633 operations per evaluated F9 claw: 733 + sum over the 200 groups of (110 + 403 x blocks), a formula of the table evaluated and asserted by the program, with no folded or claw-specialised code. A survivor costs 711 + 563 per class tested, at most 5,215; a key hit at most 49,472 (the at most 8 classes of its group as mates); the screen 4 + 183 per first-block draw plus 3 per discarded draw; the one-time setup, the rule generator included, is charged 1,107,473,556 operations. K = 10,369 is the ceiling of the screened H6 mean-work bound 591,117,427 / 57,012.41 = 10368.22; the import assertion also checks K >= 589,661,032 / 57,012.41 = 10342.68, a panel-mean sanity check of the observed mean cost per claw, not a separate upper bound.
heuristics.scope: The counted pass, survivor, key-hit and screen paths and setup of experiments/r39joint_k4.py.
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact counts of the program; the organizer run asserts the pass cost per claw, planted survivor costs and, on one screened window, the screen charge of every draw (187 kept, 190 discarded).
heuristics.limitations: The 2^30 part of the setup is an allowance for the import's other statements.

heuristics.statement: MODEL premise of this entry (screened scope). For an F8-passing listed entry of class 01 drawn uniformly over all trial (window, claw, entry) triples of the attack, windows drawn under the screened law and weighted by their trial count, in a claw passing F9 with W17 equal to the advice value, the two 39-step compressions collide along the advice differences with probability at least 2^-74.4783: the lower of the 14-run organizer pooled mean (2^-74.4594) and class-01 mean (2^-74.4783, the replica's 4 x c01 estimator) of r39-mate-01..14, rounded down, by a rule written before the class counts existed. A mean of organizer-executed runs, not a lower confidence bound. ae2d3c1c's H2-transfer (2^-74.3238, keys and designated mate) is cited only as the keys value. Model, stated plainly: the SMC carrier sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1).
heuristics.scope: Rows 18 to 38 of the advice trail after rows 0 to 17 hold, for class-01 trial entries of windows of the screened law.
heuristics.extrapolation: From 14 organizer runs (one uniform listed entry per batch, (a0, a1) by the claw model) to class-01 entries of screened windows over the whole attack. Arm J (participant-run, real unscreened claws, an entry per lane) gives 2^-74.3828.
heuristics.limitations: A mean, not a bound: the one-sided 99.9% lower bound of the pooled runs is 2^-74.6588. The class-01 mean rests on 466 class-01 hits.

heuristics.statement: A[8..11], E[12..15] and W12..W15 are fixed to the advice values; (A[6], A[7]) range over the listed entries of the fibre 0x3cc9eebe; for every listed entry both messages follow the advice state-difference trail through step 15, W9 is C9 + 0x05cefde0 - a1 and W16 is one value per claw. Constructing and selecting the advice pair costs at most 2^43 compressions (2^42.545 by the accounting of proof Section 9), added to the claimed time; the offline fibre search costs at most about 2^31.1 compressions (estimated from the tools' loop counts), inside the remaining 2^41.1.
heuristics.scope: The one-time construction of the 160-byte advice pair of 5f8e6192; the list is generated at import by the rule of proof Section 2.5.
heuristics.extrapolation: Exhaustive enumeration over all 2^32 a3 with the real two-message trail checked on every entry at four points (0 failures); the rule reproduces that list exactly; the organizer run checks one entry of every group at the advice point.
heuristics.limitations: The 93-pair campaign was run by the pair's authors and is charged at its declared cost.

heuristics.statement: Screened-window scope: for the windows of the screened law, windows are independent (fresh first blocks, each drawn and screened independently). Trials are listed entries passing F8 in a claw passing F9: at least 10701.9 per distinct claw (measured on 10,000 F9 claws of 80 screened windows); W17 is shared by the mates of a key, so hits are counted on keys; mu_D <= 576,819 keys per F9 claw on the screened claws. Each listed key's W17 event has probability 2^-32 in each claw (a uniform claw constant); events in different claws are independent. Within a claw, two keys hit together iff G(a2, kappa, w) = s0(a2 + w) - (a2 + w) + kappa coincide. Let N_k(w) be the number of other listed keys with G equal to key k's at the claw's w, and pi_k = E_w[N_k(w)]. Measured over all 3,462,264 listed keys on two independent sets of 16,384 random w: mean pi 1.07e-3, largest per-key estimate 4.6e-3; per-(key, w) counts on the second set: N = 1 in 60,723,478 cases, N = 2 in 37,173, N = 3 in 40, N >= 4 in none of 5.67e10. At the w of 2,000 real F9 claws of 0b62ed88's unscreened program: mean pi 1.0825e-3, largest per-(key, w) N = 3 (w15/critic_final/cohit_real.c, cohit_real_2000.txt; w and u at all 43,134 real claws in wreal.py, wreal.txt). The claw's w contains -cv5 additively, so it is uniform and independent of (a0, u) under H1-screen. Hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has more than 4 keys are left out of the second-order sum; for every kept key N_k <= 3, and E[min(N_k, 3)] <= 0.0078 for every key (a run of 65,536 random w; family-wise at 0.001 over all keys and the three runs). Left-out hits cost at most P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3 x 3,462,264 / 0.001) / 65,536 = 0.000352 per key in the first-order term (no N >= 4 for any key in 65,536 w). Both bounds hold for every key, so the within-claw term holds whatever the relation between a key's partner rate and its tail. The claw's W17 constants (w, c) are independent of the mates' tail events, as for the hit events themselves. Real 2^-32 hits: 37 key hits against 38.58 expected over the 48 windows; 3 compressed F8-passing mates against 6.85 expected (P = 0.09, disclosed). The program tests every key hit; success is priced by second-order Bonferroni over all hits on the keys' mate-union events (proof Section 7), divisor 1 - 0.073047 (including the mate term of H7-mate-joint) with the cross-claw term bounded through the cap of 1,024 claws for any correlation; no premise between the tails of different hits is used.
heuristics.scope: The amplification over 2^76.386613 windows of the screened program.
heuristics.extrapolation: F8-passing entries per F9 claw 681,102.5 (s.e. 762.6, 80 batches of 125 screened claws); F9 claws per window 902.524 (124 screened windows).
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run counts (10,000 screened claws, 80 windows). The organizer's dispersion test is a scaled spot test on four fixed groups; independence of the 2^-32 events over all groups and windows is the premise, not a measurement.

heuristics.statement: Premise H-W3-uniform: given a hit (an F8-passing entry whose pair collides along the advice differences), the entry's message word W3 is uniform over 2^32. By the exhaustive enumeration of rows 18-19 (proof Section 7, Appendix D), mate j with offset d_j can follow the advice through row 19 only if W3 lies in B_{d_j} = {W3 : Delta(W3, d_j) in D = P - P, Delta != 0}, empty for 14 of the 20 offsets and of at most 120,832 elements for the others. Hence E[X_i | T_i] = sum_j P(S_j | T_i) <= 7 x 120,832 / 2^32 = eps = 1.9693e-04 (a key has at most 7 other mates), sum over keys of P(U_k) >= (1 - eps/2) sum over entries of P(T_i), and eps/2 = 0.000099 is in the divisor. No independence between mates is assumed.
heuristics.scope: Every key hit: the program compresses every F8-passing mate (k4q); the enumeration covers every W3 and every mate offset of the list.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer test of the premise (the r39-mate manifest prediction): r39-mate-01..14 pin the W3 of all 1,888 hits (867 carrier clusters) by their organizer-recorded digest48 (proof Appendix E); 0 lie in the union of the B_d (expected 0.24; falsified at 3 or more); per-bit chi-square 24.7 on 32 df (falsified at 62.49); 638 F8-passing mates traced, none past row 19. Price without the premise (disclosed, not priced): the strict hit-weighted 99% cluster bound 0.01716 gives eps 0.12015, divisor 1 - 0.133025, time 94.1648. Not used: per-cluster 4.605 / 867 and per-hit 4.605 / 1,888.
heuristics.limitations: H-W3-uniform is a premise about one distribution (W3 given a hit); 1,888 hits test it only coarsely at the 2.8e-5 scale, and the B_d are structured sets (near 2^18 elements each). The r39-mate hits come from the replica's start-state law with the claw model for (a0, a1), one listed entry per batch, not from the attack's screened claws; the test is carried to screened claws as the entries tail is (H2-entries).

heuristics.statement: Screened whole-window bound (ae2d3c1c's method, credited). Under the H6 model (screened window totals i.i.d. over windows; normal-theory Student-t and chi-square bounds), mean work per window of the shipped attack path is at most 591,117,427 operations (one-sided 99.75%, t(123) = 2.8586 on 124 windows: mean 589,661,031.7, s.d. 5,673,399.6) against the cap 10,369 x 57,012.41 = 591,161,679.29 (margin 44,252.29 operations), and the per-window s.d. is at most 6,884,434.4 (chi-square(123, 0.0025) = 83.532); jointly 99.5%. A window total is the shipped counter over the whole window. These are bounds on the mean and s.d., not a maximum over windows. For independent windows Chebyshev bounds the probability that the cap binds before B windows by 2.46e-19 (B = 98,778,303,628,521,972,432,897).
heuristics.scope: The work cap of k4_budget for the screened program.
heuristics.extrapolation: From 124 pre-declared screened windows (ae2d3c1c's 60, this entry's 64) to 2^76.386613 windows.
heuristics.limitations: Model-based bounds on the sample moments under the stated window-distribution model.

heuristics.statement: Given the claws, the W17 events of distinct keys are dispersed as independent trials. Tested in the organizer run at a scaled event of probability 2^-7 on every key of four groups (every 50th) with an entry in F8, in every F9 claw of the four organizer windows: 146,502 key events, 1,104 hits against 1144.5 expected (z = -1.20), Pearson 19.29 on 22 claws; acceptance region fixed in the manifest and asserted.
heuristics.scope: Four of the 200 groups, all F9 claws of the four organizer windows of r39k4-window-small.
heuristics.extrapolation: The attack's event has probability 2^-32 on the same keys and words.
heuristics.limitations: Four groups only, for run time; the groups are fixed by the program.
